concerns.text: The OpenAlex dataset cited (GlobalCampus/openalex-multilingual-embeddings) contains multilingual text embeddings, not the raw 'Works' metadata (Title, Authors, DOI, Venue) required for fuzzy matching. The plan requires raw metadata to match pre-prints to journals, but this dataset only provides vector representations. The correct source is the official OpenAlex S3 'works' raw dumps or the OpenAlex API, not an embeddings dataset.

The plan assumes 'Direct download (PDF URL from metadata)' for arXiv/bioRxiv and journal publishers. While arXiv provides stable PDF URLs, major journal publishers (Elsevier, Springer, Wiley) do not provide direct, unauthenticated PDF download links via public APIs or metadata dumps. Relying on 'Direct download' for a large-scale pipeline (N=1000) will fail due to paywalls, CAPTCHAs, or dynamic URL generation, making the extraction step infeasible without a specific, accessible source strategy (e.g., Unpaywall, CORE, or specific open-access subsets).

The plan states 'PDFs will be downloaded one at a time and processed sequentially to stay within the 7GB RAM limit.' However, downloading 1000+ PDFs sequentially on a GitHub Actions free-tier runner (2 CPU, ~7GB RAM) with a 6-hour timeout is infeasible. Network latency and PDF parsing overhead will likely exceed the time limit. The plan must account for parallelization (within rate limits) or a significantly smaller sample size, or acknowledge that the 6-hour target is unachievable with sequential I/O.
